title: Usage watermark realignment and graceful burst servo for reserved quotas
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Reserved capacity customers occasionally observe unexpected early throttling or silent billing adjustments when hourly/daily rolling watermarks drift relative to tenant-local activity patterns. Root causes include tenant timezone drift, intermittent delayed usage ingestion, small negative reconciliation patches, and aggressive bucket smoothing policies that shrink burst capacity during backfills. These behaviors cause surprising customer outages and billing disputes for customers on Reserved and Dedicated plans.

Goal: Implement a deterministic watermark realignment flow plus a transient "burst servo" that allows short, bounded bursts without perturbing long-window quotas. The solution should preserve accounting correctness (no double-counting), be idempotent for replay, and be compatible with existing reserved pool mechanics and billing ledger. It must offer observability and an opt-out for high-precision billing accounts.
acceptance_criteria: New watermark realignment job runs incrementally per-tenant without creating duplicate ledger entries
Burst servo permits configurable short bursts (default 10s at 1.5x) for Reserved tenants without altering monthly allocation or invoiceable usage
All quota adjustments are accounted in audit logs with reasons (delay_backfill | timezone_shift | servo_grant)
No regressions in existing quota reset behavior; e2e smoke tests pass for midnight and rolling-window resets across timezones
Dashboard shows per-tenant realignment delta distribution and burst servo grants for first 30 days
implementation_notes: Introduce tenant_watermark table: (tenant_id, last_aligned_epoch_iso, pending_offset_seconds, idempotency_token) - stored as ledger-friendly records (append-only) to avoid in-place edits

Realignment flow: 1) compute expected watermark from consumption ledger and tenant timezone; 2) compute delta; 3) emit compensating ledger record (type=watermark_realignment) when delta > threshold; 4) tag records with idempotency token and origin=realignment-job

Burst servo logic lives in quota-evaluator: when instantaneous token bucket exhausted, evaluate servo policy (recent healthy headroom, SLA tier) and optionally grant short-lived soft-credit that is capped and labelled for later reconciliation
Ledger implications: servo grants are tracked as non-invoiceable credits by default and reconciled monthly; billing-only-tenants can opt-in to mark servo grants as invoiceable via billing policy
Conflict resolution: realignment jobs should use optimistic compare-and-swap against last_aligned_epoch_iso to avoid race with concurrent backfills
API: expose GET /quota/realignment-status and POST /quota/servo-config for admins (console+API)
rollout_plan: Feature flag: quota.watermark_realignment_v1 and quota.burst_servo_v1 (default off for <enterprise> tenants)
Phase 1 (canary): enable both features for internal test orgs and 5 low-traffic Reserved customers; run for 2 weeks and collect telemetry
Phase 2 (limited): enable for small set of Reserved customers that opt-in via support process; monitor billing deltas and dispute rates
Phase 3 (general): enable for all Reserved tenants after 30 days of stable metrics; turn on by default but allow per-tenant opt-out for strict-billing customers
Fallback: if realignment introduces >0.5% unexpected invoiceable delta in canary, roll back realignment job and switch to diagnostic-only mode
telemetry_and_metrics: SLOs: average realtime-latency for quota-evaluator < 15ms, and realignment job latency p95 < 5s per-tenant
Dashboards: Realignment heatmap (tenant vs delta), Servo grants timeline, Billing delta cohort analysis
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency token generation and ledger emission
Integration tests simulating delayed ingestion (5m, 1h, 6h) with expected compensating ledger entries
Chaos test: concurrent backfill + realignment job on same tenant to verify CAS behavior
End-to-end across timezones: simulated tenants in UTC±12 to validate midnight rolling-window behavior
Billing smoke: verify servo grants are non-invoiceable by default, and invoiceable when tenant billing policy set
Manual QA checklist for Support: reproduction steps, mitigation commands (disable servo, trigger forced alignment)
migration_steps: Run one-off migration to create tenant_watermark table, backfill last_aligned_epoch_iso from ledger tombstones
Backfill small sample of tenants with >1h drift to validate delta computation; hold realignment_job in dry-run mode for 72h
Add gateway feature flags and console controls before enabling for any customer
Communicate to customers: Support bulletin documenting opt-in/opt-out and expected invoice effects
